1. demographic (adj / n)
/ˌdem.əˈɡræf.ɪk/
(Thuộc về) nhân khẩu học; cấu trúc dân số theo độ tuổi, giới tính, nơi ở.
Collocation: demographic transition / demographic shift
Ex: "Developing countries are undergoing a profound demographic transition as birth rates decline."
2. urbanisation (n)
/ˌɜː.bən.aɪˈzeɪ.ʃən/
Sự đô thị hóa; quá trình chuyển dịch dân cư từ nông thôn ra thành thị.
Collocation: unprecedented urbanisation / rapid urbanisation
Ex: "Unprecedented urbanisation in Southeast Asia has placed immense strain on water resources."
3. megacity (n)
/ˈmeɡ.ə.sɪt.i/
Siêu đô thị (thành phố có quy mô dân số trên 10 triệu người).
Collocation: sprawling megacity / emerging megacities
Ex: "Tokyo remains the world's most populous megacity, housing over 37 million residents."
4. infrastructure (n)
/ˈɪn.frəˌstrʌk.tʃər/
Cơ sở hạ tầng cơ bản (giao thông, mạng lưới điện nước, trường học, bệnh viện).
Collocation: transport infrastructure / upgrade civic infrastructure
Ex: "Heavy municipal investment is required to modernise antiquated transport infrastructure."
5. exponential (adj)
/ˌek.spəˈnen.ʃəl/
Tăng theo cấp số nhân; tăng vọt với tốc độ ngày càng dồn dập.
Collocation: exponential growth / increase exponentially
Ex: "Urban energy consumption has experienced exponential growth over the past three decades."
6. surpass (v)
/səˈpɑːs/
Vượt trội hơn; vượt qua một mức số liệu hoặc kỷ lục trước đó.
Collocation: surpass initial projections / surpass the previous record
Ex: "By 2030, the metropolitan population is forecast to surpass twenty million inhabitants."
7. plateau (v / n)
/ˈplæt.əʊ/
Chững lại ở mức cao sau một thời kỳ tăng trưởng mạnh; trạng thái bình ổn.
Collocation: reach a plateau / plateau at approximately 75%
Ex: "After a dramatic surge in the 1990s, urbanization rates in Europe have plateaued at 80%."
8. fluctuate (v)
/ˈflʌk.tʃu.eɪt/
Dao động liên tục; biến thiên lên xuống không ổn định.
Collocation: fluctuate erratically / moderate fluctuations
Ex: "Migration rates to coastal metropolises fluctuated erratically during the economic recession."
9. plummet (v)
/ˈplʌm.ɪt/
Lao dốc, sụt giảm mạnh và đột ngột (từ vựng Task 1 cao cấp).
Collocation: plummet drastically / plummet to an all-time low
Ex: "Rural employment figures plummeted drastically following the mechanisation of agriculture."
10. stabilise (v)
/ˈsteɪ.bəl.aɪz/
Bình ổn trở lại; giữ ở trạng thái ổn định và cân bằng.
Collocation: gradually stabilise / stabilise at a manageable level
Ex: "Population growth is expected to stabilise once national fertility rates reach replacement levels."
11. density (n)
/ˈden.sə.ti/
Mật độ dân số; độ dày đặc của người hoặc vật thể trong một đơn vị diện tích.
Collocation: high population density / density per square kilometre
Ex: "High population density in inner districts exacerbates air pollution and housing deficits."
12. sprawl (n / v)
/sprɔːl/
Sự mở rộng tràn lan vô trật tự của thành phố ra các vùng ngoại ô.
Collocation: unchecked urban sprawl / curb suburban sprawl
Ex: "Strict zoning regulations are introduced to curb uncontrolled urban sprawl into agricultural land."
13. inhabitant (n)
/ɪnˈhæb.ɪ.tənt/
Cư dân cư trú; người sinh sống lâu dài tại một địa bàn (paraphrase của resident/citizen).
Collocation: urban inhabitants / long-term inhabitants
Ex: "Over half of the world's inhabitants now dwell in metropolitan and urban centres."
14. overburden (v)
/ˌəʊ.vəˈbɜː.dən/
Tạo áp lực quá tải; đè nặng gánh nặng lên hệ thống dịch vụ công.
Collocation: overburden public services / overburden the healthcare system
Ex: "Sudden population influxes severely overburden local sanitation and hospital systems."
15. projection (n)
/prəˈdʒek.ʃən/
Số liệu dự báo mang tính thống kê khoa học cho tương lai.
Collocation: statistical projection / according to current demographic projections
Ex: "According to UN demographic projections, Asia will house several new megacities by 2040."
16. disparity (n)
/dɪˈspær.ə.ti/
Sự phân hóa, bất bình đẳng sâu sắc giữa hai nhóm đối tượng hoặc khu vực.
Collocation: wealth disparity / regional economic disparity
Ex: "Widening economic disparity between rural provinces and capital cities fuels mass migration."
17. congestion (n)
/kənˈdʒes.tʃən/
Tình trạng tắc nghẽn giao thông hoặc quá tải cục bộ.
Collocation: severe traffic congestion / ease vehicular congestion
Ex: "The expansion of subway networks is vital to alleviate chronic vehicular congestion."
18. depopulation (n)
/diːˌpɒp.jəˈleɪ.ʃən/
Sự suy giảm dân số nghiêm trọng (thường xảy ra ở vùng nông thôn khi người trẻ bỏ đi).
Collocation: rural depopulation / severe depopulation of farming hamlets
Ex: "Many agricultural towns face severe rural depopulation as young graduates seek urban careers."
19. sustainable (adj)
/səˈsteɪ.nə.bəl/
Bền vững; đáp ứng nhu cầu hiện tại mà không làm tổn hại đến tương lai.
Collocation: sustainable urban development / environmentally sustainable models
Ex: "Architects are prioritizing green roofs and renewable energy to build sustainable communities."
20. predominantly (adv)
/prɪˈdɒm.ɪ.nənt.li/
Chiếm ưu thế tuyệt đối; phần lớn, chủ yếu.
Collocation: predominantly rural / predominantly urbanised region
Ex: "A century ago, the global population was predominantly rural and engaged in agrarian labor."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

• 1. Cặp Cấu Trúc Động Từ vs Danh Từ: 'The population increased significantly' (V + Adv) ⟷ 'There was a significant increase in the population' (There was a/an + Adj + N + in).

• 2. Đa Dạng Hóa Từ Chỉ Tốc Độ & Biên Độ: Dramatic / Sharp / Steep (mạnh mẽ); Steady / Moderate / Gradual (đều đặn, vừa phải); Marginal / Slight (nhẹ, không đáng kể).

• 3. Ngôn Ngữ Dự Báo Tương Lai (Projections): 'is projected / predicted / forecast to reach X' hoặc 'is anticipated to see an upward trend'.

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions


Paragraph A
For the vast majority of human history, our species was predominantly agrarian and rural. As late as 1800, fewer than ten percent of human beings lived in settlements that could plausibly be termed cities. However, the onset of the Industrial Revolution catalyzed an unprecedented demographic upheaval. The mechanisation of agricultural machinery dramatically diminished the demand for farm labor, triggering widespread rural depopulation across Western Europe. Simultaneously, emerging textile factories, shipping docks, and coal-fired steel mills in urban centers generated a voracious demand for human workforce, magnetizing millions of impoverished rural inhabitants to expanding cities.

Paragraph B
Today, humanity has irrevocably crossed an evolutionary threshold. According to statistical projections released by the United Nations Population Division, over 56 percent of the world's population currently resides in metropolitan conurbations, a metric forecast to surpass 68 percent by 2050. This surge is creating a new geographic phenomenon: the megacity. In 1950, only New York and Tokyo surpassed the ten-million-inhabitant threshold. By 2025, there were more than 33 recognized megacities, and demographers anticipate that this number will expand exponentially, particularly across the Global South. Emerging powerhouses such as Dhaka, Lagos, and Kinshasa are expanding at rates that challenge conventional urban engineering.

Paragraph C
This explosive concentration of populace creates both profound socioeconomic opportunities and alarming structural vulnerabilities. On the economic ledger, high population density fosters remarkable agglomeration efficiencies. Dense metropolises generate more patents, attract larger venture capital investments, and produce greater economic output per capita than smaller townships. By concentrating educational institutions, research hospitals, and corporate headquarters within accessible transit radii, megacities serve as engines of national innovation and global trade integration.

Paragraph D
Conversely, the negative externalities of unchecked expansion are acute. When urbanization outpaces municipal planning, cities succumb to chronic urban sprawl, transforming fertile green belts into vast suburban peripheries lacking water mains, public schools, or sewage treatment. The resulting vehicle reliance causes catastrophic vehicular congestion and toxic air pollution that shortens life expectancy. Furthermore, sudden population growth threatens to overburden public healthcare systems and municipal housing stocks, widening the socio-economic disparity between fortified luxury compounds and informal hillside slums.

Paragraph E
The central governance challenge of the coming century is therefore not to prevent urbanisation—an endeavor history suggests is both futile and economically counterproductive—but to render it environmentally sustainable. Progressive municipal authorities in cities like Curitiba, Singapore, and Copenhagen demonstrate that strategic civic investment can decouple demographic density from ecological degradation. By prioritizing high-capacity electrified mass transit, enforcing mandatory green building insulation standards, and revitalizing blue-green civic infrastructure, cities can house millions of inhabitants while reducing per-capita environmental footprints. The future of human civilisation will decisively be won or lost in our megacities.
Điểm: 0/6
